sarrus-linkage.note: Real products using a true Sarrus linkage are scarce; both examples are patented industrial designs rather than catalogue products.

real_world.product: Automated mooring robot (US patent 12325494)
real_world.use: A Sarrus linkage between base and attachment element lets the mooring pad extend straight out from the quay toward the ship while fully supporting its weight and retracting to a small footprint.

real_world.product: Flexure linear-motion stage (US patent 9879974)
real_world.use: Monolithic flexure stage that builds on two Sarrus double-arm linkages set at 90 degrees to guide a carriage along a straight line without bearings.

tusi-couple.note: Rare in products; the surviving Murray engine is the classic real machine, plus a modern prototype engine using the same 2:1 hypocycloid (Cardan) gear.

real_world.product: Matthew Murray's hypocycloidal steam engine (c.1805), Thinktank Birmingham Science Museum
real_world.maker: Matthew Murray / Fenton, Murray and Wood
real_world.use: A planet gear rolling inside a ring of twice its diameter guides the piston rod end in a straight line and turns it into crankshaft rotation, replacing a crosshead guide.

real_world.product: Wiseman hypocycloid engine alpha prototype (30cc two-stroke)
real_world.use: A 2:1 internal gear hypocycloid keeps piston and connecting rod moving in a straight line; the built prototype was dynamometer tested at MTD Southwest.

real_world.product: Gould & Eberhardt 16 inch industrial universal shaper
real_world.use: A real shop shaper whose ram is driven from the bull gear crank with the Eberhardt quick-return mechanism so the ram returns faster than it cuts.

real_world.product: Gould & Eberhardt 16 inch shaper restoration reference
real_world.use: Describes the ram driven by a crank or bull gear in the column body, including crank-pin bearing wear that causes a thumping stroke.

real_world.product: Atlas 7B bench shaper teardown and rebuild
real_world.use: Photo teardown of a real shaper showing the crank gear, crank pin and sliding block, and crank arm that drive the ram.

real_world.product: Warner & Whitney vertical metal shaper (1872), American Precision Museum
real_world.use: The crank is driven through double gearing and a Whitworth quick-return motion so the vertical ram cuts slowly and returns fast.

real_world.product: Whitworth crank planing machine (c.1850), Musee des Arts et Metiers, Paris
real_world.use: The crank-driven planer table has the quick-return motion credited to Whitworth.

drag-link-quick-return.note: No current catalogue product found naming a drag-link quick return; examples are press-drive prior art from Bliss and a historic museum model of a drag-link mechanism.

real_world.product: Drag-link mechanical press drive (prior art in US patent 4107973)
real_world.use: In drag-link presses the crank drives the slide through a drag link that slows the slide on the working stroke for a mechanical advantage of up to 5:1.

real_world.product: Reuleaux model: drag-link orientation mechanism (Morgan feathering paddle wheel), 1882
real_world.use: Four-bar drag-link arms drive feathering paddles as on steam paddle boats, a double-crank drag-link chain in physical form.

real_world.product: Honda K20C1 engine (Civic Type R)
real_world.use: The crankshaft is offset relative to the bores so the connecting rod is more upright on the power stroke, reducing piston side thrust and friction.

real_world.product: Yamaha MT-09 CP3 three-cylinder engine
real_world.use: The cylinder bores are offset 5 mm toward the exhaust side of the crank to reduce friction between pistons and cylinder walls.

real_world.product: Walschaerts valve gear from double Fairlie locomotive Snake (1874), National Railway Museum
real_world.use: The actual right-hand valve gear from a New Zealand 0-4-4-0T, believed among the first British-built locomotives with Walschaerts gear.

real_world.product: LNER Peppercorn A1 class and new-build 60163 Tornado
real_world.use: Three independent sets of Walschaerts valve gear control steam admission to the three cylinders.

bennett-linkage.note: No commercial products; both examples are built large-scale research prototypes.

real_world.product: 8 m span deployable Bennett-linkage arch shelter prototype
real_world.maker: University of Oxford, Department of Engineering Science
real_world.use: Tiled Bennett linkages with nylon hinges and carbon fibre tubes form a 49 kg arch that folds for transport and is erected by a small team.

real_world.product: Deployable parabolic cylindrical antenna prototype
real_world.use: A network of Bennett linkages deploys the antenna support structure with a single degree of freedom; a physical prototype was constructed.

real_world.product: Rexroth A10VSO 71 DFR series 31 axial piston variable pump
real_world.use: An adjustable swashplate sets piston stroke so the pump varies its displacement and flow.

real_world.product: Robinson R44 helicopter swashplate (Service Bulletin SB-10)
real_world.use: Upper and lower swashplates with scissor linkages pass cyclic and collective pitch from the stationary controls to the rotating main rotor blades.

real_world.product: Sanden swash plate automotive A/C compressor
real_world.use: A swash plate on the belt-driven shaft reciprocates several pistons to compress refrigerant for passenger car air conditioning.

real_world.product: PI P-733.Z high-dynamics Z nanopositioner
real_world.use: Zero-play flexure guides with lever amplification give 100 micrometre piezo-driven travel without friction or backlash.

real_world.product: Free-Flex flexural pivots
real_world.use: Crossed-spring flexure pivot bearings give frictionless, lubrication-free limited rotation in gimbals, sensors and aerospace linkages.

bistable-compliant.note: Bistable compliant parts in products are rarely documented as such; the slap bracelet is a bistable tape-spring shell and flip-top closures use a snap hinge.

real_world.product: Slap bracelet (originally sold as Slap Wrap)
real_world.use: Layered bistable stainless steel spring bands stay straight until slapped, then snap into a stable curled state around the wrist.

real_world.product: Aptar Flip Lid beverage closure
real_world.use: A moulded 270 degree lockage hinge snaps the lid open and closes it with an audible click; the snap-hinge behaviour is implied, not stated as bistable.

real_world.product: Boulton and Watt rotative steam engine (Lap Engine), 1788, Science Museum
real_world.use: The first engine fitted with the centrifugal governor, whose flyballs throttle steam to hold engine speed.

real_world.product: Woodward PG dial and lever governors
real_world.use: A centrifugal flyweight head and pilot valve control oil to a power cylinder that sets the fuel rack of diesel and gas engines.

real_world.product: Ford Instrument Company five-inch disc integrator (Smithsonian NMAH)
real_world.use: Two stacked steel balls on a movable carriage between a disc and a cylinder integrate inputs in U.S. Navy gun fire control computers.

real_world.product: Kelvin's Harmonic Analyser (1878), Science Museum
real_world.maker: R W Munro and Company, design by Lord Kelvin
real_world.use: Seven discs turned by the tracing point drive rolling spheres that pass integrated motion to the recording rollers to extract harmonic coefficients.

real_world.product: Manchester University differential analyser (1935), Science Museum
real_world.use: Four disc-and-wheel integrators (the wheel variant, not ball) chained to solve differential equations.

real_world.product: MTD snow blower friction wheel 935-0243B
real_world.use: A rubber friction wheel rides on the drive plate and is shifted across it to set speed and direction of the snow blower wheels.

real_world.product: 1914 Metz Model 22 Roadster
real_world.use: A friction-drive transmission with a driven disc and movable friction wheel gives variable ratio without gears.

real_world.product: 1913 Metz driving review
real_world.use: Drive of a real 1913 Metz whose friction transmission pairs a paper disc with an aluminium disc as a manual CVT.

real_world.product: Nissan XTRONIC CVT
real_world.use: Two variable-width pulleys change the running radius of a steel belt to vary the ratio continuously.

real_world.product: Bosch CVT pushbelt
real_world.use: Hundreds of steel elements held by steel bands push between the variator pulleys of car CVTs.

real_world.product: DAF 600 Variomatic
real_world.use: V-section rubber belts run on split cone pulleys whose halves move apart or together to change ratio automatically.
